Name: target_cluster_downsample_budget
Title: Target-Cluster Budget: cap=0 with Fair Matched Control
Experiment: Six-condition protocol: cap=0; matched_random_embedding samples N=embedding target cluster; matched_random_linguistic samples N=linguistic target cluster; all_mixed uses full pool (ceiling). Verify clustering beats its paired matched control on low_resource_macro_f1 / average_f1.

Name: head_final_cohesion
Title: Constrained Clustering: Keep ja-ko-mn Together for East-Asian Transfer
Experiment: Modify cluster_embedding() so ja, ko, mn must share one cluster (hard or soft constraint) before/during agglomerative clustering. Cap500 floor: embedding groups {ja,ko,mn} but still loses to matched_random on pool transfer. Add cohesion constraint. Success: embedding_clustering beats matched_random on low_resource_macro_f1; mn F1 is secondary evidence.

Name: script_aware_mn_ru_penalty
Title: Script-Aware Typology Distance: Penalize Cyrillic Script Confusion
Experiment: Extend _hybrid_lang_distance_matrix() with an extra penalty when pairing typologically distant languages that share script (e.g. mn-ru). Goal: improve cluster purity and pool-wide transfer, not mn-only tuning. Tune penalty weight. Compare embedding vs matched_random on low_resource_macro_f1 and per-language F1.

Name: typology_weighted_mixture
Title: Soft Typology-Weighted Training Mixture Instead of Hard Cluster Cut
Experiment: Replace hard langs_in_cluster() selection with typology-based language weights across the pool. Sample or weight training sentences proportional to typology similarity to each eval language (or cluster centroid). Still report as embedding_clustering regime. Target: beat matched_random on low_resource_macro_f1 and pool macro F1.

Name: k2_silhouette_head_final
Title: Silhouette k Selection with k>=2 and HEAD_FINAL Merger
Experiment: Change _select_k_by_silhouette() to search k in {2,3,4} with optional typology-prior merge so related East-Asian languages co-locate. Addresses pathological splits without abandoning data-driven k. Evaluate pool-wide transfer vs matched_random.

Name: low_resource_reweight
Title: Low-Resource Stratum Reweighting in Transfer Mixtures
Experiment: Implement augment_train_raw(): up-weight sentences from low_resource_macro_f1 stratum languages within selected transfer languages (not mn-only). Improves low-resource transfer without changing cluster assignment logic. Success: low_resource_macro_f1 > matched_random.

Name: typology_guided_diversity_expansion
Title: Typology-Guided Diversity Expansion: Using Linguistic Distance to Grow, Not Shrink, the Training Pool
Experiment: Do NOT modify cluster_linguistic() or cluster_embedding(); they MUST keep producing the exact same base cluster as the floor run (e.g. {ja,ko,mn} for both). NOTE: on this pool, cluster_embedding() already coincides with cluster_linguistic() at this base cluster because cluster_embedding() is itself a typology-penalized hybrid, not a pure embedding method (see notes.txt / experiment.py docstring). Because of this, matched_random_embedding's N is BY DEFINITION already equal to the base cluster's N (floor protocol samples matched controls to the clustering condition's own size) -- there is NO room to grow N by adding languages on top of the full base cluster without exceeding the matched N. Therefore diversity must be introduced by REPLACEMENT, not addition: implement augment_train_raw() to swap out a fraction R of the base cluster's sentences and replace them with an equal number of sentences from other pool languages, keeping total n_train_samples exactly equal to the base cluster's N (and thus to matched_random's N) at every value of R, by construction (removed count == added count). Use SOURCE-SPECIFIC ranking to choose which sentences/languages to bring in: for source='linguistic', rank candidates by pure linguistic/typological distance (URIEL/lang2vec features only, no embeddings) from the base cluster; for source='embedding', rank candidates by pure sentence-embedding distance (no typology penalty term) from the base cluster centroid. Sweep the replacement ratio R across the 5 runs: R must be monotonically increasing across runs, with no repeated value, spanning from near-0% (close to floor) to near-100% (close to matched_random), with at least 4 distinct values (e.g. R roughly 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 90%, but you may choose different specific values as long as monotonicity/no-duplication/spread hold). Whether to implement the replacement at the sentence level (embed and rank individual candidate sentences from the pool) or at the language level (rank whole candidate languages and swap in their sentences) is your design choice; note the sentence-level approach requires embedding the full ~192k-sentence pool once (reusable across all 5 runs) and is more compute-intensive. Before reporting any run, assert that final n_train_samples equals the matched control's N for that run; if they differ, treat the run as invalid and fix the code rather than reporting it. Also verify before each run that its R value and resulting language distribution genuinely differ from every previous run in this experiment -- do not repeat a configuration already tested. Success: embedding_clustering and/or linguistic_clustering (with replacement) beats matched_random on low_resource_macro_f1 and/or average_f1 at some value of R, at equal N throughout.
